subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity should define the default inbound-media isolation boundary for multi-agent/channel deployments?
rationale: Current source proves the flat store remains, but choosing account-, agent-, session-, or tenant-scoped paths affects security guarantees, plugin API shape, compatibility, cleanup, and explicit media-sharing behavior.

options.title: Define a generic scoped media contract first
options.body: Choose a core media identity/provenance contract, then update bundled/plugin media saves, managed URI resolution, sandbox staging, cleanup, docs, and regression coverage around that contract.

options.title: Use account-id directories only
options.body: This is the narrowest implementation but may not match multi-tenant or multi-agent bindings where one account can route to multiple agents or where explicit sharing is needed.

options.title: Leave the flat store and document operator isolation
options.body: This avoids compatibility churn but keeps the reported privacy and correctness failure mode as an operator responsibility.

recommendation.title: Define a generic scoped media contract first
recommendation.body: Choose a core media identity/provenance contract, then update bundled/plugin media saves, managed URI resolution, sandbox staging, cleanup, docs, and regression coverage around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest routing candidate from original media-store history, security/staging work, and the prior maintainer review on this issue.
